name: abuse
title: Abuse 2.00 (Crack dot Com, 1996), from Debian 2.0's abuse 2.00-11 source
fetch: mkdir -p corpus/abuse/debian-src corpus/abuse/debian-lib/x corpus/abuse/debian-lib/data && curl -Lo corpus/abuse/debian-src/abuse_2.00.orig.tar.gz http://archive.debian.org/debian/dists/hamm/main/source/games/abuse_2.00.orig.tar.gz && curl -Lo corpus/abuse/debian-src/abuse_2.00-11.diff.gz http://archive.debian.org/debian/dists/hamm/main/source/games/abuse_2.00-11.diff.gz && tar -xzf corpus/abuse/debian-src/abuse_2.00.orig.tar.gz -C corpus/abuse/debian-src && cp -R corpus/abuse/debian-src/abuse-2.00.orig corpus/abuse/debian-src/abuse-2.00 && gunzip -c corpus/abuse/debian-src/abuse_2.00-11.diff.gz | patch -p1 -d corpus/abuse/debian-src/abuse-2.00 && curl -Lo corpus/abuse/debian-lib/abuse-lib_2.00-5.deb http://archive.debian.org/debian/dists/hamm/main/binary-i386/games/abuse-lib_2.00-5.deb && (cd corpus/abuse/debian-lib/x && ar x ../abuse-lib_2.00-5.deb) && tar -xzf corpus/abuse/debian-lib/x/data.tar.gz -C corpus/abuse/debian-lib/data
_doc: Crack dot Com's own source, released to the public domain in 1997, as Debian 2.0 (hamm) built it: abuse_2.00.orig.tar.gz with Debian's abuse_2.00-11.diff.gz applied, as dpkg-source -x does -- the source of the abuse 2.00-11 binary that MIRAGE-LINUX can run, the cross-oracle. The patch is Joey Hess's (1997) and is what let Debian ship the game without Bobby Prince's non-free sound effects: the release's cache.c exits when a .wav is missing, the patched one goes on; it also pins PATH/ABUSE_PATH (the binary was setgid games) and drops a mem_report that crashed without sound. The shareware levels, art and Lisp are Debian's abuse-lib 2.00-5 (public domain, Dave Taylor's 1997 letter in its copyright file).
_units: The game and imlib units both platforms build (abuse/Makefile.am's abuse_x11R6_SOURCES, abuse/makefile.wat's gameo objects, imlib's libraries); each variant adds its platform's port and network driver.
_compile: Every unit is a .c compiled by $(CXX): the Makefiles' COMPILE rule.
_defines: MYDEFS in both builds' rules: -DMANAGE_MEM -DNO_CHECK (the opt build's).

x11.title: Abuse 2.00: Debian 2.0's abuse.x11R6 (Linux, X11)
x11._doc: abuse/Makefile.am's abuse.x11R6, linked with the imlib libraries configure picks on Linux: libsound (readwav.c + port/sgi/sound.c -- configure's choice for *-linux, the SGI driver talking to lnx_sdrv), libdir (port/unix/jdir.c), libjoy (port/linux/joystick.c), libtime (port/unix/timing.c), libwinman (port/x11 + jwindow.c). Not libnet (port/unix/jnet.c): abuse_x11R6_LDADD's IMLIBS does not link it, and listing it defined net_uninit twice.
x11._defines: MYDEFS (MANAGE_MEM, NO_CHECK), and what configure finds on Debian 2.0: HAVE_ATEXIT (AC_CHECK_FUNCS(atexit on_exit, break) stops at the first). NOT NO_XSHM: configure looks for XShmAttach in libXext first, and finds it, so the MIT-SHM path is compiled in; PRISM's X server then says the extension is absent at run time, as a remote server would, and Abuse takes XPutImage. __linux__ as gcc predefines it on Linux: Abuse tests it (6 places).
x11._args: debian/wrapper's: -nosound when /var/lib/games/abuse/sfx is absent, which it is (abuse-sfx is non-free).
x11._run: --data=<abuse-lib> --mount=/var/lib/games/abuse --exact --cwd=/var/lib/games/abuse, as Debian installs it and debian/wrapper starts it; --input="wait 50; click 47 166" passes the gamma screen.

dos4gw.title: Abuse 2.00: the DOS build (Watcom C++ 10, DOS/4GW)
dos4gw._doc: abuse/makefile.wat's gameo.exe (the opt build) as game.lnk links it: the game's objects with src/net/dos4gw/ipx.c for its network, and imlib's Watcom libraries image, winman (port/dos4gw video, mouse, event, doscall + jwindow.c), gui, dir, time, sound (port/dos4gw/sound.c, readwav.c, profile.c), joy, packet. NOT HMI's SOS (c:\sos\lib\sosw1cr.lib): a commercial library the release does not carry -- its functions are left undefined and the game runs -nosound, which never calls them.
dos4gw._defines: __WATCOMC__ and __386__ are wpp386's identity macros, which the source tests in 33 places. HAVE_ATEXIT: exitproc.hpp, written for the autoconf build, demands it or HAVE_ON_EXIT; makefile.wat defines neither, and Watcom's library has atexit.
dos4gw._compile: /zp1 in every opt rule: byte alignment, so every struct changes size -- including the .spe files' headers it reads. C++ as Watcom C++ 10 took it: the pre-standard rules (compiler "watcom", src/cxx/index.js).
dos4gw._sound: imlib's own no-sound driver (port/unix/sound.c) where the sound library's port/dos4gw/sound.c stood: that one is written against HMI's SOS SDK (sos.h, sosm.h, sosw1cr.lib), which the release does not carry, and profile.c reads SOS's configuration for it alone. A departure, stated: the game runs -nosound either way.
dos4gw._systemIncludesFirst: makefile.wat's `set include=$(%WATCOM)\h;inc;../imlib/include;...`: Watcom's own headers before the tree's, so <dos.h> is Watcom's and not imlib/include/dos.h (which the X11 build, gcc -I, does mean).
dos4gw._dir: The release as Crack dot Com shipped it, abuse_2.00.orig.tar.gz untouched: Debian's patch is the Linux package's (its game.c pins ABUSE_PATH to /var/lib/games/abuse/ on every platform), so the DOS build takes the tree it was written in.
